info.description:
Kaapi is Project Tech4Dev’s AI platform designed to accelerate responsible AI adoption across the global development ecosystem. Acting as a middleware layer, it enables platforms like Avni, Glific, Evidential, and Dalgo to seamlessly integrate AI functionality- without each having to build or maintain their own infrastructure.

Kaapi will support NGOs with end-to-end AI workflows: conversation management, sector-specific co-pilots, input classification, document handling, and multi-language/multi-modal support—all guided by responsible AI practices

item.name: Errors & Troubleshooting
item.description:
# Errors & Troubleshooting — Evaluation APIs

All Evaluation, STT Evaluation, and TTS Evaluation endpoints return a structured `APIResponse` envelope. On success, `success: true` and `data` carries the payload. On error, the HTTP status code reflects the error class and the body contains a `detail` (or `error`) field with a human-readable message.

## HTTP status codes you may see

| Status | Meaning | Common causes (Evaluation domains) | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | Bad request | Empty dataset, missing Langfuse ID, unsupported audio format, audio > 200 MB, dataset has no samples, TTS feedback on non-`SUCCESS` result, conflicting query params on Get Evaluation Run, duplicate dataset name in STT/TTS, `file_id` not found in STT dataset create | Fix the request body / query and retry |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid `X-API-KEY` header | Set the `API_KEY` collection variable |
| 403 | Forbidden | API key lacks `REQUIRE_PROJECT` permission, or the resource belongs to a different org/project | Use a key bound to the correct org+project |
| 404 | Not found | Dataset / run / sample / result / file ID does not exist in this org/project, or `language_id` not found | Verify the ID; check it was created in this scope |
| 409 | Conflict | Text-eval dataset name already exists in this org/project (after sanitization) | Choose a different name |
| 413 | Payload too large | CSV upload > 1 MB (text eval) | Split the CSV or trim it; the limit is fixed |
| 422 | Unprocessable entity | CSV missing required columns, invalid CSV MIME, empty file, sanitized name became empty, config provider not `openai`, empty `samples` list, TTS text > 5000 chars / whitespace-only, unsupported `models` value | Fix the payload per the message |
| 500 | Internal server error | Langfuse upload failure, object-storage upload failure, batch queue failure | Retry; if persistent, ping the platform team |

## High-traps to know

1. **`"models": ["string"]` will 422.** The previous Postman scaffold shipped this. Use `gemini-2.5-pro` (STT) or `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts` (TTS).
2. **TTS feedback on non-`SUCCESS` results returns 400.** Confirm `status` is `SUCCESS` before PATCHing.
3. **`get_trace_info=true` on a non-completed run** doesn't error with HTTP — it returns the run with a soft message in the body (`Trace info is only available for completed evaluations. Current status: …`). Don't panic.
4. **`resync_score=true` requires `get_trace_info=true`** (and `export_format=grouped` requires `get_trace_info=true`). Otherwise both return 400.
5. **Dataset name sanitization is silent.** `"My Dataset 01!"` becomes `"my_dataset_01"`. Always read the name back from the API response.
6. **Signed URLs expire after 1 hour.** Re-fetch the resource with `include_signed_url=true` if a URL has expired.
7. **Failed runs surface the cause via `error_message`** — both at run level and per-result. Always read this field when `status == failed`.
8. **All run processing is asynchronous via Celery + Gemini Batch API.** Poll the GET endpoint every 30–60 seconds; never tighter than 5 seconds.

## Capability gaps (not supported via API today)

- Cancelling an in-flight evaluation run
- Retrying a failed run without reconstructing the request body
- Deleting STT or TTS datasets (text-eval datasets do have DELETE)
- Renaming a dataset
- Appending samples to an existing dataset
- Bulk human feedback in a single call
- CSV/JSON results export
- Webhook / push notification on completion — client must poll

## Authentication

The collection-level auth attaches `X-API-KEY: {{API_KEY}}` to every request. Set `API_KEY` in the environment variables before sending any request. All endpoints under Evaluation/STT/TTS require this header and are scoped to the org+project that owns the key.

request.description:
List all _active_ collections that have been created and are not deleted.

**Response Fields:**

**Note:** While the API schema shows both `llm_service_id`/`llm_service_name` AND `knowledge_base_id`/`knowledge_base_provider`, each collection in the response will only include the fields relevant to what was created:

- **If an Assistant was created** (with model + instructions): The response will only include `llm_service_id` and `llm_service_name` (e.g., `llm_service_name: "gpt-4o"` and the assistant ID)
    
- **If only a Vector Store was created** (without model/instructions): The response will only include `knowledge_base_id` and `knowledge_base_provider` (e.g., `knowledge_base_provider: "openai vector store"` and the vector store ID)

Setup and configure the document store that is pertinent to the RAG pipeline:

- Create a vector store from the document IDs you received after uploading your documents through the Documents module.
    
- The `batch_size` parameter controls how many documents are sent to OpenAI in a single transaction when creating the vector store. This helps optimize the upload process for large document sets. If not specified, the default value is **10**.
    
- \[Deprecated\] Attach the Vector Store to an OpenAI [Assistant](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/assistants). Use parameters in the request body relevant to an Assistant to flesh out its configuration. Note that an assistant will only be created when you pass both "model" and "instruction" in the request body otherwise only a vector store will be created from the documents given.
    

If any one of the LLM service interactions fail, all service resources are cleaned up. If an OpenAI vector Store is unable to be created, for example, all file(s) that were uploaded to OpenAI are removed from OpenAI. Failure can occur from OpenAI being down, or some parameter value being invalid. It can also fail due to document types not being accepted. This is especially true for PDFs that may not be parseable.

In the case of Openai, Vector store/assistant will be created asynchronously. The immediate response from this endpoint is `collection_job` object which is going to contain the collection "job ID" and status. Once the collection has been created, information about the collection will be returned to the user via the callback URL. If a callback URL is not provided, clients can check the `collection job info` endpoint with the `job_id`, to retrieve information about the creation of collection.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific collection by its collection id. This endpoint returns the collection object including its project, organization, timestamps, and service-specific details.  
  

**Response Fields:**

**Note:** While the API schema shows both `llm_service_id`/`llm_service_name` AND `knowledge_base_id`/`knowledge_base_provider`, the actual response will only include the fields relevant to what was created:

- **If an Assistant was created** (with model + instructions): The response will only include `llm_service_id` and `llm_service_name`
    
- **If only a Vector Store was created** (without model/instructions): The response will only include `knowledge_base_id` and `knowledge_base_provider`
    

**Including Documents:**

If the `include_docs` flag in the parameter is true then you will get a list of document IDs associated with a given collection as well. Note that, documents returned are not only stored by Kaapi, but also by Vector store provider.

Additionally, if you set the `include_url` parameter to true, a signed URL will be included in the response, which is a clickable link to access the retrieved document. If you don't set it to true, the URL will not be included in the response.

Retrieve information about a collection job by the collection job ID. This endpoint provides detailed status and metadata for a specific collection job in Kaapi. It is especially useful for:

- Fetching the collection job object, including the collection job ID, the current status, and the associated collection details.
    
- If the job has finished, has been successful and it was a job of creation of collection then this endpoint will fetch the associated collection details.
    
- If the delete-collection job succeeds, the status is set to "successful" and the `collection` key contains the ID of the collection that has been deleted.
    

**Response Fields for Successful Creation Jobs:**

**Note:** While the API schema shows both `llm_service_id`/`llm_service_name` AND `knowledge_base_id`/`knowledge_base_provider`, the actual collection object in the response will only include the fields relevant to what was created:

- **If an Assistant was created** (with model + instructions): The response will only include `llm_service_id` and `llm_service_name`
    
- **If only a Vector Store was created** (without model/instructions): The response will only include `knowledge_base_id` and `knowledge_base_provider`

item.name: Config & Version Management

request.description:
Create a new LLM configuration with an initial version.

Configurations allow you to store and manage reusable LLM parameters (such as temperature, max_tokens, model selection, etc.) with version control.

**Key Features:**

- Automatically creates an initial version (v1) with the provided configuration
    
- Enforces unique configuration names per project
    
- Stores provider-specific parameters as flexible JSON (config_blob)
    
- Supports optional commit messages for tracking changes
    
- Kaapi providers (`openai`, `google`, `sarvamai`) — params are validated and mapped internally
    
- Native providers (`openai-native`, `google-native`, `sarvamai-native`) — params are passed through as-is
    
- Supports three completion types: `"text"`, `"stt"` and `"tts"`
    
- Supports both `input_guardrails` and `output_guardrails`
    

**Example for the config blob: OpenAI Responses API with File Search -**

```
"config_blob": {
  "completion": {
    "provider": "openai",
    "type": "text",
    "params": {
      "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
      "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant for farming communities...",
      "temperature": 1,
      "knowledge_base_ids": [
        "vs_692d71f3f5708191b1c46525f3c1e196"
      ]
    }
  }
}

 ```

**Example for the config blob: Google gemini STT -**

```
"config_blob":{
  "completion": {
    "provider": "google",
    "type": "stt",
    "params": {
      "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
      "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant ...",
      "input_language": "english",
      "output_language": "hindi",
      "temperature": 1
    }
  }
}

 ```

**Example for the config blob: Google gemini TTS -**

```
"config_blob":{
  "completion": {
    "provider": "google",
    "type": "tts",
    "params": {
      "model": "gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts",
      "voice": "Kore",
      "language": "hindi",
      "response_format": "mp3"
    }
  }
}

 ```

The configuration name must be unique within your project. Once created, you can create additional versions to track parameter changes while maintaining the configuration history.

**Provider–type support:**

- `openai` / `openai-native` — `"text"`
    
- `google` / `google-native` — `"text"`, `"stt"`, `"tts"`
    
- `sarvamai` / `sarvamai-native` — `"stt"`, `"tts"`

Query: Search string used for partial matching across configurations skip: Number of records to skip for pagination (default: 0) limit: Maximum number of records to return (default: 100, max: 100)

Retrieve all configurations for the current project.

Returns a paginated list of configurations ordered by most recently updated first. Each configuration includes metadata (name, description, timestamps) but excludes version details for performance.

Retrieve a specific configuration by its ID.

Returns the configuration metadata including name, description, and timestamps. This endpoint provides configuration-level details but does not include version information.

Update a configuration's metadata (name or description).

This endpoint modifies only the configuration-level metadata, not the LLM parameters themselves. To change LLM parameters, create a new version instead.

Delete a configuration and all its versions.

This operation performs a delete, marking the configuration and all associated versions as deleted in the database while retaining records for audit purposes.

Create a new version for an existing configuration.

To create a new version, provide the `config_id` in the URL path and the new configuration parameters in the request body. The system will automatically create a new version under the same configuration with an incremented version number. Version numbers are automatically incremented sequentially (1, 2, 3, etc.) and cannot be manually set or skipped.

## Important

- This endpoint accepts partial updates using dict\[str, Any\] for `config_blob`.
    
- Only the fields that need to be updated should be provided.
    
- The `type` field is inherited from the existing configuration and cannot be changed. Provider and model can change between versions.

List all versions for a specific configuration.

Returns versions in descending order (newest first), allowing you to see the evolution of configuration parameters over time.

Retrieve a specific version of a configuration.

Returns the complete version details including the full configuration blob (config_blob) with all LLM parameters.  
  
Add/Update the `config_id` and `version_number` in the URL.

Delete a specific version of a configuration.

Performs a delete on the version, marking it as deleted while retaining the record for audit purposes.

Add/Update the `config_id` and `version_number` in the URL.

item.name: Evaluation

request.description:
# Getting Started — Text / LLM Evaluation

This walkthrough takes you from zero to a completed text-eval run using only API calls. Replace `<API_KEY>` with your `X-API-KEY` value (or set the `{{API_KEY}}` collection variable once).

## Lifecycle

```
[Create config] → [Upload dataset] → [Start run] → [Poll status] → [Fetch scores]
```

## Step 1: Create or pick a config

You need a stored config whose `completion.provider == "openai"`. Use the **Config & Version Management** folder to create one. Note the `config_id` (UUID) and `config_version` from the response.

## Step 2: Upload a dataset

Prepare a CSV with exactly two columns: `question`, `answer`. Maximum **1 MB**.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -F 'file=@qa.csv' \
  -F 'dataset_name=customer_support_v1' \
  -F 'duplication_factor=1' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/datasets
```

The response includes `dataset_id`. Note it. The `dataset_name` may have been sanitized; use the value returned by the API for future calls.

## Step 3: Start the evaluation run

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "dataset_id": 42,
    "experiment_name": "gpt4_baseline",
    "config_id": "f54f0d67-4817-4103-9fdf-b74b3d46733e",
    "config_version": 1
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations
```

The response returns the run ID. Note it.

## Step 4: Poll for completion

Poll every 30–60 seconds:

```bash
curl -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/<run_id>
```

Wait until `status` is `completed`. If `status` is `failed`, read `error_message` for the cause.

## Step 5: Fetch detailed scores

```bash
curl -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  'https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/<run_id>?get_trace_info=true&export_format=row'
```

First call fetches from Langfuse and caches to S3. Subsequent calls return the cached data. Use `&resync_score=true` to force a re-fetch after evaluators are added.

## What's not supported yet

- Cancelling an in-flight run
- Retrying a failed run (you must call POST `/evaluations` again with the same body)
- Bulk feedback / per-trace edits via API (use Langfuse UI)
- CSV/JSON export of results via API (use the trace data from step 5)
- Webhook notifications on completion — client polling only

## Troubleshooting

See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection.

request.description:
Upload a CSV file containing golden Q&A pairs for evaluation.

Datasets allow you to store reusable question-answer pairs for systematic LLM testing with automatic validation, optional duplication for statistical significance, and Langfuse integration.

**Authentication:** All Evaluation endpoints require the `X-API-KEY` header (configured at the collection level via the `{{API_KEY}}` variable). Requests are scoped to the organization and project that own the API key.

**Key Features**
- Validates CSV format and required columns (`question`, `answer`)
- Automatic dataset-name sanitization for Langfuse compatibility (spaces/special chars → underscores, lowercased)
- Optional item duplication for statistical significance (1–5×, default `1`)
- Uploads to object store and syncs with Langfuse
- Skips rows with missing values automatically

**CSV Format**
- Required columns (case-insensitive): `question`, `answer`
- Extra columns are **not** allowed — request will be rejected with 422
- Rows with empty `question` or `answer` are silently skipped

**Limits**
- Maximum file size: **1 MB**
- Allowed MIME types: `text/csv`, `application/csv`, `text/plain`
- File extension must be `.csv`

**Form fields**
- `file` (required, file): CSV file with `question` and `answer` columns
- `dataset_name` (required, text): Will be sanitized for Langfuse (e.g. `"My Dataset 01!"` → `"my_dataset_01"`). Read the response to see the final name.
- `description` (optional, text)
- `duplication_factor` (optional, integer 1–5, default `1`)

**Sample CSV**
```
question,answer
What is your refund policy?,Refunds are processed within 7 business days.
How do I reset my password?,Click 'Forgot password' on the login screen.
```

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `422` — CSV missing/extra columns, empty file, missing filename, invalid MIME or extension
- `413` — File larger than 1 MB
- `409` — Dataset name already exists in this org/project (after sanitization)
- `500` — Langfuse upload failure (e.g. Langfuse credentials not configured)

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

request.description:
List all evaluation datasets for the current organization and project.

Returns a paginated list ordered by most recent first. Each entry includes the dataset ID, sanitized name, item counts (original and after duplication), duplication factor, Langfuse dataset ID, and object store URL.

**Query parameters**
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1–100, default `50`)
- `offset` (optional, integer, ≥0, default `0`)

**Response shape**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": [
    {
      "dataset_id": 42,
      "dataset_name": "customer_support_v1",
      "description": "100 FAQs from customer support tickets",
      "total_items": 300,
      "original_items": 100,
      "duplication_factor": 3,
      "langfuse_dataset_id": "clxxxxxxxxx",
      "object_store_url": "s3://..."
    }
  ]
}
```

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

Get details of a specific dataset by its database ID.

Returns dataset metadata, Langfuse integration details, and the object store URL for the CSV file.

**Path parameter**
- `dataset_id` (integer, required) — database ID returned by Upload Dataset

**Query parameter**
- `include_signed_url` (optional, boolean, default `false`) — when `true`, the response includes a time-limited signed URL for downloading the CSV directly from object storage. Signed URLs expire after **1 hour**.

**Errors**
- `404` — Dataset not found in this org/project

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

Delete a dataset by its database ID.

Removes the dataset record from the database. The underlying CSV in object storage is retained for audit purposes but the dataset will no longer be available for new evaluation runs.

**Cascade behaviour**
- Past evaluation runs that referenced this dataset remain readable — their `dataset_id` becomes a dangling reference but their results, scores, and metadata are preserved.
- The Langfuse dataset is **not** automatically deleted from Langfuse.

**Path parameter**
- `dataset_id` (integer, required)

**Errors**
- `404` — Dataset not found in this org/project
- `400` — Deletion failed (rare; database integrity issue)

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

Start an evaluation run using the OpenAI Batch API.

Evaluations systematically test an LLM configuration against a predefined dataset. Processing is asynchronous via the OpenAI Batch API; use `GET /evaluations/{evaluation_id}` to monitor progress and retrieve results.

**Authentication:** All Evaluation endpoints require the `X-API-KEY` header (configured at the collection level via the `{{API_KEY}}` variable). Requests are scoped to the organization and project that own the API key.

**Prerequisites**
1. Upload a dataset via `POST /evaluations/datasets` and note the `dataset_id`.
2. Create a config via `POST /configs` and note its `config_id` (UUID) and `config_version`. The config's `completion.provider` **must be `openai`** — other providers are rejected with `422`.
3. Ensure Langfuse credentials are configured for the project (the dataset needs a Langfuse dataset ID).

**Request body**
```json
{
  "dataset_id": 123,
  "experiment_name": "gpt4_file_search_v1",
  "config_id": "f54f0d67-4817-4103-9fdf-b74b3d46733e",
  "config_version": 1
}
```

**Field details**
- `dataset_id` (integer, required)
- `experiment_name` (string, required) — friendly name shown alongside runs in Langfuse
- `config_id` (UUID, required)
- `config_version` (integer, required, ≥1)

**What happens next**
1. The dataset's items are fetched from Langfuse.
2. A batch processing job is created via the OpenAI Batch API.
3. Status is updated to `processing`; a background worker polls every 60 s.
4. On completion, scores are computed and stored. Poll the **Get Evaluation Run Status** endpoint to retrieve them.

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `404` — Dataset not found in this org/project
- `400` — Dataset has no Langfuse ID (Langfuse credentials were missing when the dataset was created); config cannot be resolved
- `422` — Config provider is not `openai`
- `500` — Failed to enqueue the batch job

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

List all evaluation runs for the current organization and project.

Returns a paginated list ordered by most recent first. Each run includes ID, name, dataset reference, config reference, status, total items, batch job IDs, scores (when available), cost, and timestamps.

**Query parameters**
- `limit` (optional, integer, default `50`)
- `offset` (optional, integer, default `0`)

**Status enum**
- `pending` — run record created, batch not yet submitted
- `processing` — batch is running on OpenAI
- `completed` — results ready; query the run for scores
- `failed` — read the `error_message` field on the run for the cause

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

request.description:
Get the current status and results of a specific evaluation run.

Returns evaluation metadata, processing status, configuration references, progress metrics, and (optionally) Langfuse trace scores with full Q&A context. Use this endpoint to poll an in-flight run and to fetch final scores.

**Polling guidance:** Evaluation runs are processed asynchronously by a background worker. Poll this endpoint every 30–60 seconds until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. Do not poll faster than once per 5 seconds.

**Status lifecycle:** `pending` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`.

**Path parameter**
- `evaluation_id` (integer, required) — ID returned by the start endpoint

**Query parameters**
- `get_trace_info` (optional, default `false`) — include Langfuse trace scores with Q&A context. **Only available when `status == completed`**; calling it on an in-flight run returns the run with a soft error in the response body (`Trace info is only available for completed evaluations. Current status: …`).
- `resync_score` (optional, default `false`) — clear cached scores and re-fetch from Langfuse. Useful when evaluators have been added or updated since the last call. **Requires `get_trace_info=true`** (otherwise returns `400`).
- `export_format` (optional, default `row`, allowed: `row`, `grouped`) — controls the structure of `traces`. `grouped` collates repeated questions horizontally using parent question ID. **`grouped` requires `get_trace_info=true`** (otherwise returns `400`).

**Reading a failed run**
When `status == failed`, read the top-level `error_message` field on the run for the cause. Common reasons: OpenAI batch quota exceeded, dataset became unavailable in Langfuse, embedding job failure.

**Score Format** (`get_trace_info=true`, `export_format=row`)
```json
{
  "summary_scores": [
    {
      "name": "cosine_similarity",
      "avg": 0.87,
      "std": 0.12,
      "total_pairs": 50,
      "data_type": "NUMERIC"
    },
    {
      "name": "response_category",
      "distribution": {"CORRECT": 10, "PARTIAL": 5, "INCORRECT": 2},
      "total_pairs": 17,
      "data_type": "CATEGORICAL"
    }
  ],
  "traces": [
    {
      "trace_id": "uuid-123",
      "question": "What is 2+2?",
      "llm_answer": "4",
      "ground_truth_answer": "4",
      "scores": [
        {"name": "cosine_similarity", "value": 0.95, "data_type": "NUMERIC"},
        {"name": "correctness", "value": 1, "data_type": "NUMERIC", "comment": "Response is correct"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Score Format** (`get_trace_info=true`, `export_format=grouped`)
Same shape as above but `traces` becomes:
```json
[
  {
    "question_id": 1,
    "question": "What is Python?",
    "ground_truth_answer": "Python is a high-level programming language.",
    "llm_answers": ["Answer from run 1...", "Answer from run 2..."],
    "trace_ids": ["uuid-123", "uuid-456"],
    "scores": [
      [{"name": "cosine_similarity", "value": 0.82, "data_type": "NUMERIC"}],
      [{"name": "cosine_similarity", "value": 0.75, "data_type": "NUMERIC"}]
    ]
  }
]
```

**Score details**
- NUMERIC scores include `avg` and `std` in summary; values rounded to 2 dp
- CATEGORICAL scores include distribution counts in summary
- Only complete scores are included (all traces have been rated)
- First fetch from Langfuse is cached to S3; subsequent reads serve from cache for speed. Use `resync_score=true` to bypass the cache.

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `404` — Run not found or not accessible to this org/project
- `400` — `resync_score=true` without `get_trace_info=true`
- `400` — `export_format=grouped` without `get_trace_info=true`

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

Initiate fine-tuning of an OpenAI model using a CSV dataset. The CSV must include:

- A column named `query`, `question`, or `message` containing user inputs or messages.
    
- A column named `label` indicating whether a given message is a genuine query or not (e.g., casual conversation or small talk).
    

The `split_ratio` form field is a comma-separated string that determines how your data is divided between training and testing. For example, `"0.5"` means 50% training and 50% testing. You can provide multiple ratios—for instance, `"0.7,0.9"`. This will trigger multiple fine-tuning jobs, one for each ratio. You would also need to specify a `base_model` that you want to fine-tune.

The `system_prompt` form field allows you to define an initial instruction or context-setting message that will be included in the training data. This message helps the model learn how it is expected to behave when responding to user inputs. It is prepended as the first message in each training example during fine-tuning.

The system handles the fine-tuning process by interacting with OpenAI's APIs under the hood. These include:

- [Openai File create to upload your training and testing files](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/files/create)
    
- [Openai Fine Tuning Job create to initiate each fine-tuning job](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/fine_tuning/create)
    

If successful, the response will include a message along with a list of fine-tuning jobs that were initiated. Each job object includes:

```
{
    "id": "the internal ID of the fine-tuning job",
    "document_id": "the ID of the document used for fine-tuning",
    "split_ratio": "the data split used for that job",
    "status": "the initial status of the job (usually 'pending')"
}

 ```

request.description:
Make an LLM API call using either a stored configuration or an ad-hoc configuration.

This endpoint initiates an asynchronous LLM call job. The request is queued for processing, and results are delivered via the callback URL when complete.

### Key Parameters

**`query`** (required) - Query parameters for this LLM call:

- **`input`** (required) — User input in one of three forms:
    
    1. "input": "Hello"
        
    2. "input": {"type": "text", "content": {"format": "text", "value": "Hello"}}
        
    
    - **List of structured inputs** — for multimodal use cases (supports `image`, `pdf`, and `text`; `audio` is only supported as a single structured input)
        
    
    **Supported input types:** `text`, `audio`, `image`, `pdf`
    
    **Content format by type:**
    
    - `text` — format: `"text"`
        
    - `audio` — format: `"base64"`, optional `mime_type` (e.g. `audio/wav`)
        
    - `image` — format: `"base64"` or `"url"`, optional `mime_type` (default: `image/png`)
        
    - `pdf` — format: `"base64"` or `"url"`, optional `mime_type` (default: `application/pdf`)
        
    
    For `image` and `pdf`, `content` can be a single object or a list of objects.
    
- **`conversation`** (optional) — Conversation configuration
    
    - `id` (string): Existing conversation ID to continue
        
    - `auto_create` (boolean, default false): Create a new conversation if no ID provided
        
    - **Note**: Cannot specify both `id` and `auto_create=true`
        

**`config`** (required) - Configuration for the LLM call (just choose one mode):

- **Mode 1: Stored Configuration**
    
    - `id` (UUID): Configuration ID
        
    - `version` (integer >= 1): Version number
        
    - **Both required together**
        
    - **Note**: When using stored configuration, do not include the `blob` field in the request body
        
- **Mode 2: Ad-hoc Configuration**
    
    - `blob` (object): Complete configuration object
        
        - `completion` (required, object): Completion configuration
            
            - `provider` (required, string): Provider type — `"openai"` or `"google"` (Kaapi abstraction), or `"openai-native"` or `"google-native"` (pass-through)
                
            - `type` (required, string): Completion type — `"text"`, `"stt"`, `"tts"`
                
            - `params` (required, object): Parameters structure depends on provider and type (see schema for detailed structure)
                
        - `input_guardrails` (optional, list)
            
        - `output_guardrails` (optional, list)
            
    - **Note**
        
        - When using ad-hoc configuration, do not include `id` and `version` fields
            
        - When using the Kaapi abstraction, parameters that are not supported by the selected provider or model are automatically suppressed. If any parameters are ignored, a list of warnings is included in the metadata.warnings. For example, the GPT-5 model does not support the temperature parameter, so Kaapi will neither throw an error nor pass this parameter to the model; instead, it will return a warning in the metadata.warnings response.
            
    - **Recommendation**: Use stored configs (Mode 1) for production; use ad-hoc configs only for testing/validation
        
    - **Schema**: Check the API schema or examples below for the complete parameter structure for each provider type
        

**`callback_url`** (optional, HTTPS URL):

- Webhook endpoint to receive the response
    
- Must be a valid HTTPS URL
    
- If not provided, response is only accessible through job status
    

**`include_provider_raw_response`** (optional, boolean, default false):

- When true, includes the unmodified raw response from the LLM provider
    

**`request_metadata`** (optional, object):

- Custom JSON metadata
    
- Passed through unchanged in the response
    

### Note

- `warnings` list is automatically added in response metadata when using Kaapi configs if any parameters are suppressed or adjusted (e.g., temperature on reasoning models)

Retrieve the status and results of an LLM call job by job ID.

This endpoint allows you to poll for the status and results of an asynchronous LLM call job that was previously initiated via the POST `/llm/call` endpoint.

### Notes

- Add/Update the `job_id` in the URL.
    
- This endpoint returns both the job status AND the actual LLM response when complete
    
- LLM responses are also delivered asynchronously via the callback URL (if provided)
    
- Jobs can be queried at any time after creation

Execute a chain of LLM calls sequentially, where each block's output becomes the next block's input.

This endpoint initiates an asynchronous LLM chain job. The request is queued for processing, and results are delivered via the callback URL when complete.

### Key Parameters

**`query`** (required) - Initial query input for the first block in the chain:

- `input` (required): User question/prompt/query — accepts a plain string, a structured input object (`text`, `audio`, `image`, `pdf`), or a list of structured inputs
    
- `conversation` (optional, object): Conversation configuration
    
    - `id` (optional, string): Existing conversation ID to continue
        
    - `auto_create` (optional, boolean, default false): Create new conversation if no ID provided
        
    - **Note**: Cannot specify both `id` and `auto_create=true`
        

**`blocks`** (required, array, min 1 block) - Ordered list of blocks to execute sequentially. Each block contains:

- `config` (required) - Configuration for this block's LLM call (just choose one mode):
    
    - **Mode 1: Stored Configuration**
        
        - `id` (UUID): Configuration ID
            
        - `version` (integer >= 1): Version number
            
        - **Both required together**
            
        - **Note**: When using stored configuration, do not include the `blob` field in the request body
            
    - **Mode 2: Ad-hoc Configuration**
        
        - `blob` (object): Complete configuration object
            
            - `completion` (required, object): Completion configuration
                
                - `provider` (required, string): Kaapi providers (`openai`, `google`, `sarvamai`) — params are validated and mapped internally. Native providers (`openai-native`, `google-native`, `sarvamai-native`) — params are passed through as-is
                    
                - `type` (required, string): Completion type — `"text"`, `"stt"`, or `"tts"`
                    
                - `params` (required, object): Parameters structure depends on provider and type (see schema for detailed structure)
                    
            - `input_guardrails` (optional, array): Guardrails applied to validate/sanitize input before the LLM call
                
            - `output_guardrails` (optional, array): Guardrails applied to validate/sanitize output after the LLM call
                
            - `prompt_template` (optional, object): Template for text interpolation
                
                - `template` (required, string): Template string with `{{input}}` placeholder — replaced with the block's input before execution
                    
        - **Note**
            
            - When using ad-hoc configuration, do not include `id` and `version` fields
                
            - When using the Kaapi abstraction, parameters that are not supported by the selected provider or model are automatically suppressed. If any parameters are ignored, a list of warnings is included in the metadata.warnings.
                
        - **Recommendation**: Use stored configs (Mode 1) for production; use ad-hoc configs only for testing/validation
            
        - **Schema**: Check the API schema or examples below for the complete parameter structure for each provider type
            
- `include_provider_raw_response` (optional, boolean, default false):
    
    - When true, includes the unmodified raw response from the LLM provider for this block
        
- `intermediate_callback` (optional, boolean, default false):
    
    - When true, sends an intermediate callback after this block completes with the block's response, usage, and position in the chain
        

**`callback_url`** (optional, HTTPS URL):

- Webhook endpoint to receive the final response and intermediate callbacks
    
- Must be a valid HTTPS URL
    
- If not provided, response is only accessible through job status
    

**`request_metadata`** (optional, object):

- Custom JSON metadata
    
- Passed through unchanged in the response
    

### Note

- If any block fails, the chain stops immediately — no subsequent blocks are executed
    
- `warnings` list is automatically added in response metadata when using Kaapi configs if any parameters are suppressed or adjusted (e.g., temperature on reasoning models)

item.name: STT Evaluation

request.description:
# Getting Started — STT (Speech-to-Text) Evaluation

This walkthrough takes you from zero to a completed STT-eval run using only API calls.

## Lifecycle

```
[Upload audio (×N)] → [Create STT dataset] → [Start STT run] → [Poll status] → [Review results] → [Submit feedback]
```

## Step 1: Upload audio files

One call per file. Supported formats: `mp3`, `wav`, `flac`, `m4a`, `ogg`, `webm`. Max **200 MB** per file.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -F 'file=@recording-01.mp3' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/stt/files
```

Each response returns a `file_id`. Collect all of them.

## Step 2: Create the STT dataset

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "hindi_call_center_v1",
    "description": "100 samples from call-center recordings",
    "language_id": 5,
    "samples": [
      { "file_id": 7225, "ground_truth": "hello how can I help you" },
      { "file_id": 7226, "ground_truth": "my order number is 12345" }
    ]
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/stt/datasets
```

`language_id` can be looked up via the **Languages** folder.

## Step 3: Start the STT run

Currently exactly one model is supported: `gemini-2.5-pro`.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "run_name": "baseline_run_2024_q4",
    "dataset_id": 1909,
    "models": ["gemini-2.5-pro"]
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/stt/runs
```

## Step 4: Poll for completion

Poll every 30–60 seconds:

```bash
curl -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/stt/runs/<run_id>
```

Status moves `pending → processing → completed | failed`.

## Step 5: Review results

Once `completed`, the response includes `results`. Each result has a `transcription`, `score` (WER/CER/MER/WIL when ground truth is set), and per-result `status`.

## Step 6: Submit human feedback

For each result you reviewed:

```bash
curl -X PATCH \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"is_correct": true, "comment": "matches ground truth"}' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/stt/results/<result_id>
```

## What's not supported yet

- DELETE for STT datasets
- Adding more samples to an existing dataset (create a new one instead)
- Multiple STT models per run (single provider currently)
- Bulk feedback in a single call

## Troubleshooting

See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection.

Get a single STT transcription result by ID.

Returns the generated transcription, the provider that produced it, the result status, evaluation metrics, human feedback fields, and any error message.

**Path parameter**
- `result_id` (integer, required)

**Response shape**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": 5001,
    "transcription": "hello how can i help you",
    "provider": "gemini-2.5-pro",
    "status": "SUCCESS",
    "score": {"wer": 0.05, "cer": 0.02, "mer": 0.05, "wil": 0.08},
    "is_correct": true,
    "comment": "matches ground truth",
    "error_message": null,
    "stt_sample_id": 3001,
    "evaluation_run_id": 1909
  }
```

request.description:
# Getting Started — TTS (Text-to-Speech) Evaluation

This walkthrough takes you from zero to a completed TTS-eval run using only API calls.

## Lifecycle

```
[Create TTS dataset] → [Start TTS run] → [Poll status] → [Review audio] → [Submit feedback]
```

## Step 1: Create the TTS dataset

Texts only — no file uploads needed. Each sample text must be ≤ 5000 characters.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "customer_greetings_v1",
    "description": "Greetings for support voicebot",
    "language_id": 5,
    "samples": [
      { "text": "Welcome to Project Tech4Dev support. How may I help you today?" },
      { "text": "Your request has been received. We will get back to you within 24 hours." }
    ]
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/tts/datasets
```

## Step 2: Start the TTS run

Currently exactly one model is supported: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`. The default voice is `Kore` with a calm, professional customer-service style.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "run_name": "voicebot_qa_2024_q4",
    "dataset_id": 7653,
    "models": ["gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts"]
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/tts/runs
```

## Step 3: Poll for completion

Poll every 30–60 seconds:

```bash
curl -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/tts/runs/<run_id>
```

## Step 4: Review generated audio

Once `completed`, fetch the run with signed URLs to listen to each generated WAV:

```bash
curl -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  'https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/tts/runs/<run_id>?include_signed_url=true'
```

Each result includes `object_store_url`, `signed_url` (1-hour TTL), `duration_seconds`, and `size_bytes`.

## Step 5: Submit human feedback

**Important:** feedback is only accepted on results whose `status` is `SUCCESS`. Calling PATCH on a `PENDING` or `FAILED` result returns 400.

```bash
curl -X PATCH \
  -H 'X-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "is_correct": true,
    "comment": "clear and natural",
    "score": {
      "Speech Naturalness": "high",
      "Pronunciation Accuracy": "high"
    }
  }' \
  https://api-staging.kaapi.ai/api/v1/evaluations/tts/results/<result_id>
```

The `score` schema is **illustrative**, not enforced — you can use your own keys and values.

## What's not supported yet

- DELETE for TTS datasets
- Voice / style-prompt customization per run via API
- Multiple TTS models per run (single provider currently)
- Cancel / retry a run

## Troubleshooting

See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection.

request.description:
Update human feedback and score on a single TTS synthesis result.

**⚠️ Important:** Feedback is **only accepted when the result `status` is `SUCCESS`**. Calling this endpoint on a `PENDING` or `FAILED` result returns `400` with the message: `Cannot provide feedback on result with status '<X>'. Only completed results accept feedback.`

Only provided fields are updated. Sending a field as `null` clears its value; omitting a field leaves it unchanged.

**Path parameter**
- `result_id` (integer, required)

**Request body**
- `is_correct` (boolean | null, optional) — overall audio quality acceptable?
- `comment` (string | null, optional)
- `score` (object | null, optional) — free-form metrics. The schema below is **illustrative**, not enforced; you may choose your own keys and values.

**Example**
```json
{
  "is_correct": true,
  "comment": "clear and natural",
  "score": {
    "Speech Naturalness": "high",
    "Pronunciation Accuracy": "high",
    "Emotion Match": "medium"
  }
}
```

**Suggested score keys** (low | medium | high): `Speech Naturalness`, `Pronunciation Accuracy`, `Emotion Match`, `Speed Appropriateness`.

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `404` — Result not found in this org/project
- `400` — Result status is not `SUCCESS` (see warning above)

request.description:
Start a TTS evaluation run on an existing TTS dataset.

Each text sample is synthesized to audio by every requested model in parallel via the Gemini Batch API. Generated WAV files are stored for human review.

**Authentication:** All Evaluation endpoints require the `X-API-KEY` header (configured at the collection level via the `{{API_KEY}}` variable). Requests are scoped to the organization and project that own the API key.

**Prerequisites**
1. Create a TTS dataset via **Create TTS dataset**.

**Request body**
- `run_name` (string, required, min 1 char)
- `dataset_id` (integer, required)
- `models` (array of strings, optional, defaults to `["gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts"]`) — currently exactly **one** value is supported: `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`

**Example**
```json
{
  "run_name": "voicebot_qa_2024_q4",
  "dataset_id": 7653,
  "models": ["gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts"]
}
```

**Default voice configuration**
- Voice name: `Kore`
- Style prompt: `Read in a calm, professional customer service tone`

These defaults are applied automatically; per-run overrides are not yet supported via the API.

**Supported models (current):** `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`

**Polling guidance:** Evaluation runs are processed asynchronously by a background worker. Poll this endpoint every 30–60 seconds until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. Do not poll faster than once per 5 seconds.

**Status lifecycle:** `pending` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`.

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `404` — Dataset not found in this org/project
- `400` — Dataset has no samples
- `422` — One or more `models` values are not in the supported list
- `500` — Failed to enqueue the batch submission

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.

request.description:
Create a new TTS (Text-to-Speech) evaluation dataset from text samples.

Each sample is a plain-text string the TTS model will synthesize during a run. No file upload is required — texts are stored directly.

**Authentication:** All Evaluation endpoints require the `X-API-KEY` header (configured at the collection level via the `{{API_KEY}}` variable). Requests are scoped to the organization and project that own the API key.

**Prerequisites**
- (Optional) Find a `language_id` via the `Languages` folder's `List Languages` endpoint.

**Request body**
- `name` (string, required, 1–255 chars) — unique within org/project
- `description` (string, optional)
- `language_id` (integer, optional)
- `samples` (array, required, min 1) — list of `{text}` objects
- `samples[].text` (string, required, 1–5000 chars, not whitespace-only)

**Example**
```json
{
  "name": "customer_greetings_v1",
  "description": "Greetings for support voicebot",
  "language_id": 5,
  "samples": [
    { "text": "Welcome to Project Tech4Dev support. How may I help you today?" },
    { "text": "Your request has been received. We will get back to you within 24 hours." }
  ]
}
```

**Errors specific to this endpoint**
- `400` — Dataset name already exists in this org/project
- `404` — Provided `language_id` does not exist
- `422` — `samples` is empty, any `text` is empty/whitespace, or `text` exceeds 5000 chars

**Error responses:** See the **Errors & Troubleshooting** item at the top of this collection for the full HTTP error matrix and remediation tips.
